question.prompt: Two men at points \(R\) and \(S,\) \(76\) miles apart, set out at the same time to walk towards each other. The man at \(R\) walks uniformly at \(4\dfrac12\) miles per hour; the man at \(S\) walks at \(3\dfrac14\) miles per hour for the first hour, at \(3\dfrac34\) miles per hour for the second hour, and so on, in arithmetic progression. If the men meet \(x\) miles nearer \(R\) than \(S\) in an integral number of hours, then \(x\) is:

solutions.explanation:
The whole-hour condition sharply restricts the possible meeting point. Let \(t\) be the meeting time in hours, and let \(d_R,d_S\) be the distances walked from \(R,S\). Since the meeting point is \(x\) miles nearer \(R\),
\[
d_R+d_S=76,
\qquad d_S-d_R=x.
\]
Thus \(d_R=(76-x)/2\). Every offered choice has \(2\le x\le10\), so \(33\le d_R\le37\). The man from \(R\) walks \(\frac92t\) miles, giving
\[
\frac{22}{3}\le t\le\frac{74}{9}.
\]
The only integer in this interval is \(t=8\).

Check that the other man's motion gives a meeting at that time. His eight one-hour distances form an arithmetic progression from \(\frac{13}{4}\) to \(\frac{27}{4}\) miles. Pairing the first and last terms, then the second and next-to-last terms, gives his total distance as
\[
\frac82\left(\frac{13}{4}+\frac{27}{4}\right)=40.
\]
The man from \(R\) walks \(8\cdot\frac92=36\) miles. These distances sum to \(76\), so they do meet after eight hours. Their positive speeds make the meeting unique. Therefore
\[
x=40-36=\boxed{4\text{ miles}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Use the choices and the whole-hour condition

solutions.explanation:
Because the meeting occurs after a positive integer number \(t\) of hours, the man from \(S\) completes exactly \(t\) one-hour stages. His first hourly distance is \(\frac{13}{4}\) miles, and each subsequent hourly distance increases by \(\frac12\) mile. The last is therefore
\[
\frac{13}{4}+\frac{t-1}{2}=\frac{2t+11}{4}.
\]
Pairing terms in an arithmetic progression shows that their average is the average of the first and last terms. Hence his total distance is
\[
\frac t2\left(\frac{13}{4}+\frac{2t+11}{4}\right)
=\frac{t(t+12)}4.
\]
The man from \(R\) walks \(\frac92t\) miles. At the meeting, their distances sum to \(76\), so
\[
\frac92t+\frac{t(t+12)}4=76.
\]
Multiplying by \(4\) and factoring gives
\[
t^2+30t-304=(t-8)(t+38)=0.
\]
The root \(t=-38\) cannot represent elapsed time, leaving \(t=8\). The distances are then \(36\) miles from \(R\) and \(40\) miles from \(S\). Thus the meeting point is \(\boxed{4\text{ miles}}\) nearer \(R\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Find the meeting time algebraically
